arguments.heading: What happened at the argument
paragraphs: Mr. Feigin argued age should not be a factor in the custody test.
Ms. Blackman stated the student was 13 when taken from his classroom.
Mr. Cooper argued the Court considers only external circumstances, not mental attributes.

sections.heading: What this case is about
paragraphs: North Carolina police questioned a 13-year-old student in a closed room. The state argues age is irrelevant to the custody test. The student argues his age made the encounter coercive.

sections.heading: Why it matters
paragraphs: This case defines when police questioning requires Miranda warnings. It affects how courts evaluate the coerciveness of interrogations involving minors. The outcome shapes the rights of young people during police encounters.
